title: Line Graph Interpretation
tagline: Year 2 — Trends, turning points, rates of change and comparing two lines

introduction.overview: A line graph joins data points with line segments to show how a quantity changes over time. Rising segments show increases, falling segments show decreases, and the steepness shows the size of the change. With two or more lines you can compare trends, find where one line is above the other and where they cross. Questions ask for values, differences, percentage change, averages and trends.
introduction.placementRelevance: Line graph sets are commonly asked in company aptitude rounds, and they test whether you can read trends as well as values.
introduction.realWorldContext: Share prices, monthly sales, temperature records and website traffic are all drawn as line graphs.

learningObjectives: Read values at each point of a line
Identify rising, falling and flat segments
Compute change between months and the greatest rise or fall
Compare two lines month by month
Compute averages, ratios and percentage changes from the data

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Change = later value − earlier value. Percentage change = change ÷ earlier value × 100. Average rate of change = total change ÷ number of intervals.

coreDefinitions: Data point: a plotted value for one time period.
Trend: the overall direction of the line (rising, falling, steady).
Rate of change: change per time interval; the steeper the segment, the larger the rate.
Intersection: a point where two lines meet (equal values).
Interval: the gap between two consecutive data points.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The picture hides a table. A steep segment is just a large difference between two consecutive points. Reading a line graph is reading the table of its corners and then comparing differences.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Write each line's values in a row. Compute the differences between neighbouring values to find rises and falls. For two lines, compare month by month.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Comparing lines
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Compare values in the same month

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Projection
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Next value = last value + assumed change

mainNarrative: First convert the lines to a table. Store X sold 20, 25, 22, 30, 36 and 40 lakh in the six months; store Y sold 28, 24, 30, 28, 32 and 38 lakh.
To find the biggest rise, compute the month-to-month changes. For X they are +5, −3, +8, +6 and +4, so the greatest rise is from March to April (+8). Y fell in February (−4) and April (−2).
For a percentage change, use the earlier value as base: X rose from 20 to 40 between January and June, a 100% increase. The average monthly increase is (40 − 20) ÷ 5 = 4 lakh.
To compare lines, check month by month. X was higher than Y in February, April, May and June, which is 4 months. The two lines were closest in February (a gap of 1 lakh).
For a projection, add the stated change to the last value. If Y rises in July by the same amount as from May to June (6 lakh), July sales would be 38 + 6 = 44 lakh.

deepDiveAspects.title: Slope and steepness
deepDiveAspects.content: Equal horizontal spacing means the steepest segment is the largest vertical change. Compare segments by their differences.

deepDiveAspects.title: Trend vs fluctuation
deepDiveAspects.content: A series can rise overall while falling in some months. Quote both the trend (overall) and the fluctuations when asked.

solvedExamples.title: Greatest rise
solvedExamples.question: In which month did store X show the greatest increase in sales compared with the previous month?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: April minus March is the biggest rise.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Choosing the month of the highest sale.

solvedExamples.title: Average rate of change
solvedExamples.question: What was the average monthly increase in sales of store X from January to June?

solvedExamples.title: Two-line comparison
solvedExamples.question: In how many months was the sales of X more than the sales of Y?

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Judge by eye from the graph.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Write the values in a row, compute the differences, and use the row to answer rise, fall, steepest and trend questions.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: The biggest rise cannot be in a month where the line fell.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Trend questions test reading, not heavy arithmetic.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I find the steepest rise?
Can I compute an average rate?
